stories.title: A Summer's Reading
stories.author: Bernard Malamud (1956)
stories.setting: A poor immigrant neighborhood in New York, during a very hot summer in the 1930s (the Great Depression).
plot: George, almost 20, left school at 16. He has no job and feels ashamed.
He dreams of a better life, but he does nothing to change it.
First meeting: he lies to Mr. Cattanzara – he is 'reading about 100 books'.
First rumor: the neighbors respect him; Sophie gives him a dollar a week.
He does not read. He avoids Mr. Cattanzara.
Second meeting: Mr. Cattanzara (a little drunk) asks him to name one book. George cannot.
George hides in his room for a week. Sophie finds out and stops the money.
Second rumor: people still respect him. He lies again ('Yes, I finished') and realizes Mr. Cattanzara spread the story.
In the fall, George goes to the library, counts 100 books and sits down to read.

screens.en: George Stoyonovich is almost twenty. He left high school at sixteen, about four years ago. He has no job, and he is ashamed to tell people that he never finished school.
screens.he: ג׳ורג׳ כמעט בן 20. הוא עזב את התיכון בגיל 16, לפני כמעט ארבע שנים. אין לו עבודה, והוא מתבייש לספר שלא סיים את הלימודים.
screens.task: Choose: How old is George?
screens.fb: Almost twenty. Sixteen is the age when he left school.

screens.en: George lives with his father and his older sister, Sophie. His mother is dead. His father works in a fish market, and Sophie works in a cafeteria. They live in a small, hot apartment.
screens.he: ג׳ורג׳ גר עם אבא שלו ועם אחותו הגדולה, סופי. אמא שלו נפטרה. האבא עובד בשוק דגים, וסופי עובדת בקפטריה. הם גרים בדירה קטנה וחמה.
screens.task: Choose: Who sometimes gives George money?
screens.fb: Sophie works, takes care of the home and sometimes gives George money.

screens.en: The story takes place in a poor neighborhood in New York in the 1930s, during the Great Depression. Many families are immigrants, and good jobs are hard to find. The summer is very hot.
screens.he: הסיפור מתרחש בשכונה ענייה בניו יורק בשנות ה־30, בתקופת ״השפל הגדול״ – משבר כלכלי קשה. רוב המשפחות הן משפחות מהגרים, וקשה למצוא עבודה טובה. הקיץ חם מאוד.
screens.task: Choose: Why is it hard for George to find a good job?
opts: He has no education, and times are hard.
He lives far from the city.
He is too young to work.
screens.fb: Connect the time (the Depression) to George's situation (no education).

screens.en: During the day, George stays home, listens to the radio and reads magazines. At night he walks to a quiet park and dreams about a good job, a house and people's respect. But he does nothing to make his dreams come true.
screens.he: ביום ג׳ורג׳ נשאר בבית, מקשיב לרדיו וקורא מגזינים. בלילה הוא הולך לפארק שקט וחולם על עבודה טובה, על בית ועל כבוד. אבל הוא לא עושה שום דבר כדי להגשים את החלומות.
screens.task: Complete: George dreams about ____, but he ____.
screens.fb: Separate his dreams from his actions.

screens.en: Mr. Cattanzara lives on the next block. He works in a subway booth, giving people change, but every night he reads The New York Times from beginning to end. He is kind to George. Sometimes he comes home drunk.
screens.he: מר קטנזרה גר ברחוב הסמוך. הוא עובד בתא בתחנת הרכבת התחתית ופורט כסף לנוסעים, אבל בכל ערב הוא קורא את ״הניו יורק טיימס״ – עיתון של אנשים משכילים – מההתחלה עד הסוף. הוא נחמד לג׳ורג׳. לפעמים הוא חוזר הביתה שיכור.
screens.task: Why does George care what Mr. Cattanzara thinks?
screens.fb: He is the only adult who shows real interest in George, and George sees him as a smart man.

screens.en: Mr. Cattanzara asks George what he is doing this summer. George is ashamed, so he lies twice: he says he is waiting for a job, and he says he is reading about a hundred books from a library list. Mr. Cattanzara says they can talk about the books later.
screens.he: מר קטנזרה שואל את ג׳ורג׳ מה הוא עושה בקיץ. ג׳ורג׳ מתבייש, ולכן הוא משקר פעמיים: הוא אומר שהוא מחכה לעבודה, ושהוא קורא כמאה ספרים מרשימה של הספרייה. מר קטנזרה אומר שהם יוכלו לדבר על הספרים בהמשך.
screens.task: Was George telling the truth? Explain in one sentence.
screens.fb: No. He lies because he wants Mr. Cattanzara's respect.

screens.en: Soon, people in the neighborhood smile at George and say he is a good boy. His father and Sophie also hear about the books, and Sophie gives him a dollar a week. George thinks Mr. Cattanzara told them. He even buys some books, but he does not read them.
screens.he: מהר מאוד אנשים בשכונה מחייכים אל ג׳ורג׳ ואומרים שהוא ״בחור טוב״. גם אבא וסופי שומעים על הספרים, וסופי נותנת לו דולר בשבוע. ג׳ורג׳ חושב שמר קטנזרה סיפר להם. הוא אפילו קונה כמה ספרים, אבל לא קורא אותם.
screens.task: Choose: Why do people treat George differently?
opts: They believe he is reading the books.
screens.fb: They believe the story about his reading.

screens.en: George enjoys the respect, but he feels uncomfortable. He tries to read, but he gives up. He avoids Mr. Cattanzara and even crosses the street when he sees him.
screens.he: ג׳ורג׳ נהנה מהכבוד, אבל לא מרגיש בנוח. הוא מנסה לקרוא – ומוותר. הוא מתחמק ממר קטנזרה ואפילו עובר לצד השני של הרחוב כשהוא רואה אותו.
screens.task: What is the conflict inside George?
screens.fb: He wants respect, but he is not ready to work for it, and he is afraid of the truth.

screens.en: One night Mr. Cattanzara, a little drunk, stops George. He gives him a nickel for a lemon ice, as if George were a small child. Then he asks George to name just one book he has read. George cannot answer. Mr. Cattanzara warns him not to waste his life as he did, and walks away.
screens.he: ערב אחד מר קטנזרה, קצת שיכור, עוצר את ג׳ורג׳. הוא נותן לו מטבע כדי לקנות ״ארטיק לימון״ – כאילו ג׳ורג׳ ילד קטן. אחר כך הוא מבקש ממנו לציין שם של ספר אחד בלבד שקרא. ג׳ורג׳ לא מצליח לענות. מר קטנזרה מזהיר אותו לא לבזבז את החיים כמו שהוא עצמו עשה, והולך.
screens.task: Choose: Why does Mr. Cattanzara give George a nickel?
opts: to show that George is behaving like a child
screens.fb: Treating George like a child is a message, not a mistake.

screens.en: George is so ashamed that he stays in his room for a week. Sophie finds out that he has not read the books. She stops giving him money and calls him lazy. His father cries. This is the lowest point of the story.
screens.he: ג׳ורג׳ מתבייש כל כך שהוא נשאר בחדר שלו שבוע שלם. סופי מגלה שהוא לא קרא את הספרים. היא מפסיקה לתת לו כסף וקוראת לו עצלן. אבא שלו בוכה. זו הנקודה הנמוכה ביותר בסיפור.
screens.task: How do Sophie and the father react? Write two sentences.
screens.fb: Sophie is angry and stops the money; the father cries because he is worried.

screens.en: One hot night George goes out. To his surprise, people still respect him. Someone asks if it is true that he finished all the books, and George says yes – another lie. He understands that Mr. Cattanzara has told people that he finished the books.
screens.he: בלילה חם אחד ג׳ורג׳ יוצא החוצה. להפתעתו, אנשים עדיין מכבדים אותו. מישהו שואל אם זה נכון שסיים את כל הספרים, וג׳ורג׳ עונה ״כן״ – עוד שקר. הוא מבין שמר קטנזרה סיפר לאנשים שהוא סיים את הספרים.
screens.task: Who probably spread the new rumor, and why?
screens.fb: Mr. Cattanzara – to protect George's dignity and to push him to act. Mark this as an inference.

screens.en: One evening in the fall, George goes to the library. He counts a hundred books and sits down at a table to read. He is trembling.
screens.he: ערב אחד בסתיו ג׳ורג׳ הולך לספרייה. הוא סופר מאה ספרים ומתיישב ליד שולחן כדי לקרוא. הוא רועד – אולי מהתרגשות, אולי מפחד. הסיפור לא אומר אם יסיים את הספרים.
screens.task: Choose: What exactly does George do at the end?
screens.fb: He begins reading; the story does not say he finishes.

screens.en: At the beginning, George only dreams and lies. At the end, he finally acts. The story shows the gap between wanting something and working for it.
screens.he: בהתחלה ג׳ורג׳ רק חולם ומשקר. בסוף הוא סוף־סוף עושה משהו. הסיפור מראה את הפער בין לרצות משהו לבין לעבוד בשבילו.
screens.task: Give one contrast between the beginning and the end.
screens.fb: The answer needs evidence from the beginning and from the end.

screens.en: Mr. Cattanzara is like a mentor. He shows George respect, he challenges him at the second meeting, and it seems that he spreads the second rumor. He wants George to avoid his own mistakes.
screens.he: מר קטנזרה הוא כמו מורה דרך: הוא מכבד את ג׳ורג׳, מאתגר אותו בפגישה השנייה, וכנראה גם מפיץ את השמועה השנייה. הוא רוצה שג׳ורג׳ לא יחזור על הטעויות שלו.
screens.task: How does Mr. Cattanzara influence George? Give two actions.
screens.fb: Accept careful interpretations: 'it seems that he spread the rumor'.

screens.en: The heat in George's small room is like the pressure of his lie. The quiet park stands for his dream. The library is the place of real change. The fall is a new season – maybe a new start.
screens.he: החום בחדר הקטן הוא כמו הלחץ של השקר. הפארק השקט מסמל את החלום. הספרייה היא המקום של שינוי אמיתי. הסתיו הוא עונה חדשה – אולי התחלה חדשה.
screens.task: Choose one symbol and explain it in two sentences.
screens.fb: Name the symbol, then explain what it stands for, with an event.

screens.en: Important ideas: education, respect and self-respect, responsibility, and the chance to change. The ending is hopeful but open: we do not know if George will continue.
screens.he: רעיונות מרכזיים: השכלה, כבוד וכבוד עצמי, אחריות והאפשרות להשתנות. הסוף אופטימי אבל פתוח: אנחנו לא יודעים אם ג׳ורג׳ ימשיך.
screens.task: Does the ending prove that George will succeed?
screens.fb: No. It shows a first step; future success is not certain.

screens.en: Question: Why does George lie to Mr. Cattanzara? Build your answer in three steps: ANSWER – PROVE (an event from the story) – EXPLAIN.
screens.he: שאלת Why דורשת סיבה. בונים תשובה בשלושה צעדים: תשובה ← ראיה מהסיפור ← הסבר.
screens.task: Write three sentences.
screens.fb: Model: George lies because he is ashamed and wants Mr. Cattanzara's respect. For example, he says he is reading about a hundred books, although he is not reading at all. This shows that he cares more about how people see him than about real change.

screens.en: Fact: George tells people that he finished the books. Inference: Mr. Cattanzara spread the second rumor. In your answers, show the difference: 'We can infer that…' / 'It seems that…'.
screens.he: עובדה = כתוב בסיפור. הסקה = מבינים מהרמזים. בתשובה מסמנים הסקה במילים: We can infer that… / It seems that…
screens.task: Mark each sentence: fact or inference.
screens.fb: Separate what the story says from what we understand.

screens.t: From a sentence to a paragraph
screens.en: A 5-point answer is a short paragraph (about 60–100 words): answer, two pieces of evidence, explanation and a short ending. Use linking words: however, as a result, in addition, in other words. Write about the story in the present simple.
screens.he: בחמש יחידות התשובה היא פסקה קצרה (כ־60–100 מילים): תשובה, שתי ראיות, הסבר וסיום. שפה היא 50% מהציון – השתמשו במילות קישור וכתבו על הסיפור בזמן הווה.
screens.task: Improve a one-sentence answer into a paragraph.
screens.fb: Feedback on content (answer, understanding, evidence) and on language (vocabulary, grammar, linking words).

screens.en: Explain how the ending connects to George's main conflict. Write 80–100 words and use two events as evidence.
screens.he: עכשיו כותבים לבד. נבדוק: תשובה לשאלה, הבנה נכונה, שתי ראיות, הסבר – וגם שפה: אוצר מילים, דקדוק וסימני פיסוק.
starters: At the end of the story,
This connects to his conflict because
screens.task: Write the paragraph; then improve it after feedback.
screens.fb: Do not give full marks for 'George reads 100 books'; he only begins.

questions.q: Describe George's personality at the beginning of the story. Give two examples.
questions.ev: His days at home; the lie at the first meeting.
questions.a: At the beginning of the story, George is passive and insecure. He left school at sixteen, and now, almost four years later, he still has no job and no plan. For example, he spends most of the day in his room, and at night he walks to the park and dreams about a better life. In addition, he lies to Mr. Cattanzara because he is ashamed. This shows that George wants respect, but he is not ready to work for it.

questions.q: What happens after the first meeting with Mr. Cattanzara? Explain why this event is important.
questions.how: What happens + Why important = אירוע + משמעות.
questions.ev: The first rumor; Sophie's dollar; George avoids Mr. Cattanzara.
questions.a: After the first meeting, people in the neighborhood start to treat George with respect. They believe he is reading a hundred books, and even Sophie gives him a dollar a week. This event is important because George now enjoys respect that he has not earned. As a result, the lie becomes bigger and harder to escape, so he starts avoiding Mr. Cattanzara. In other words, the respect he wanted becomes a source of pressure.

questions.q: How does George feel during and after the second meeting? Explain why.
questions.how: How does … feel = רגש + סיבה + ראיה.
questions.ev: The nickel and the question about one book; the week in his room.
questions.a: During the second meeting, George feels ashamed and trapped. Mr. Cattanzara treats him like a small child and asks him to name just one book, but George cannot answer. After the meeting, he hides in his room for a week, because he is afraid that everyone will discover the truth. Even when Sophie shouts at him and begs him, he does not come out. This shows how deeply the lie has hurt his self-respect.

questions.q: What role does Mr. Cattanzara play in George's life?
questions.how: Role = מה הדמות עושה ואיך היא משפיעה.
questions.a: Mr. Cattanzara acts like a mentor for George. First, he shows interest in George and treats him with respect, which no one else does. Later, he challenges George and warns him not to waste his life as he did. Most importantly, it seems that he spreads the rumor that George has finished the books. In this way, he protects George's dignity and gives him a reason to start reading. Without him, George would probably not change.

questions.q: Explain the ending of the story. Does George change?
questions.how: Explain the ending = מה קורה + מה השתנה + מה לא ידוע.
questions.ev: The library scene in the fall.
questions.a: At the end, on an evening in the fall, George goes to the library, counts a hundred books and sits down to read. This is the first time he acts instead of only dreaming. However, the ending is open: the story does not tell us whether he will finish the books. In my opinion, George starts to change, because for the first time he works for the respect he already has. Still, it is only a first step.

questions.q: How does the setting (the hot summer, the poor neighborhood) add to the meaning of the story?
questions.how: Setting = זמן ומקום. מסבירים איך הם משקפים את הדמות.
questions.ev: The hot room during the week of hiding; the park; the fall.
questions.a: The setting reflects George's feelings. The story takes place during a very hot summer in a poor immigrant neighborhood in New York. When George hides in his small room, the heat makes it feel like a prison, just like his lie. On the other hand, the quiet park represents his dream of a better life. Finally, the story ends in the fall, a new season, which suggests that a new stage in his life may begin. I appreciated this, because the place helps us feel George's situation.

questions.q: Which character did you identify with most? Explain why.
questions.how: Identify with = להזדהות. בוחרים דמות, מסבירים למה, ומביאים אירוע.
questions.ev: Any accurate event connected to the chosen character.
questions.a: I identified most with George. Like him, I have sometimes said I would do something just to make people proud of me, and then I felt pressure because I had not done it yet. For example, George tells Mr. Cattanzara that he is reading a hundred books, and then he avoids him. I understand his fear of being caught. However, unlike George, I learned that it is better to tell the truth early. That is why his story feels real to me.

questions.q: Relate the story to your own life or to someone you know.
questions.how: Relate = מחברים בין הסיפור לחיים. הזכירו אירוע מהסיפור וגם מהחיים.
questions.ev: One event from the story that matches the personal example.
questions.a: The story reminds me of my cousin, who wanted to become a programmer but never practiced. Everyone told him he was talented, and he enjoyed the compliments, just like George enjoys the respect of his neighbors. However, when a friend asked him to build a simple website, he could not do it, and he felt ashamed. After that, he finally signed up for a course. Like George at the library, he took the first step only after he felt the pressure.

mistakes: He is almost twenty; he left school at sixteen.
He only begins reading at the end.
Mr. Cattanzara hates George / is cruel.
He challenges George because he cares, and he seems to protect him with the second rumor.
George stops lying after the second meeting.
He lies again when someone asks if he finished the books.
The ending shows a possible first step; the future is open.
stories.bridging: Bridging text and context: read the Ministry's background page on the Great Depression. Write 80–100 words: How does life in the 1930s help us understand George's situation and Mr. Cattanzara's warning? (CD7, CD8)

stories.title: Mr. Know-All
stories.author: W. Somerset Maugham (1925)
stories.setting: A crowded passenger ship from San Francisco to Japan, soon after World War I.
plot: After World War I, the ship is crowded; the narrator must share a cabin with Mr. Kelada.
The narrator dislikes Mr. Kelada before he even meets him (his name, his origin).
Mr. Kelada is talkative and confident; the passengers call him 'Mr. Know-All'.
At dinner, Mr. Kelada says Mrs. Ramsay's pearls are real; Mr. Ramsay says they are cheap.
They bet $100. Mr. Kelada examines the pearls and sees Mrs. Ramsay's frightened face.
He says he was wrong and pays. The passengers laugh at him.
Next morning: an envelope with $100 under the door; Mr. Kelada hints about the wife's year alone in New York.
The narrator: at that moment he did not entirely dislike Mr. Kelada.

screens.en: The story takes place soon after World War I, on a crowded ship from San Francisco to Japan. There are not enough rooms, so the narrator must share a small cabin with a stranger, Mr. Kelada.
screens.he: הסיפור מתרחש זמן קצר אחרי מלחמת העולם הראשונה, באונייה צפופה מסן פרנסיסקו ליפן. אין מספיק חדרים, ולכן המספר חייב לחלוק תא קטן עם אדם זר – מר קלדה.
screens.task: Choose: Where does most of the story happen?
screens.fb: On the ship – a small, closed place where people cannot avoid each other.

screens.en: The story is told by a first-person narrator ('I'). We see everything through his eyes, and his opinions are not always fair.
screens.he: את הסיפור מספר ״אני״ – מספר בגוף ראשון. אנחנו רואים הכול דרך העיניים שלו, והדעות שלו לא תמיד הוגנות.
screens.task: Choose: Who tells the story?
screens.fb: The narrator; remember that his view is personal.

screens.en: The narrator decides to dislike Mr. Kelada before he even meets him, because of his name and his Eastern origin. He is also annoyed by Mr. Kelada's behavior: he is too friendly, too loud and too sure of himself.
screens.he: המספר מחליט לא לאהוב את מר קלדה עוד לפני שפגש אותו – בגלל השם שלו והמוצא המזרחי שלו. הוא גם מתעצבן מההתנהגות של מר קלדה: הוא חברותי מדי, רעשן ובטוח בעצמו מדי.
screens.task: What is prejudice?
screens.fb: Judging a person before you know him, often because of his origin.

screens.en: Mr. Kelada is very talkative and sure of himself. He has an opinion about everything, and he organizes games on the ship. The passengers call him 'Mr. Know-All', even to his face.
screens.he: מר קלדה מדבר הרבה ובטוח בעצמו מאוד. יש לו דעה על כל דבר, והוא מארגן משחקים באונייה. הנוסעים קוראים לו ״מר יודע־הכול״ – אפילו בפניו.
screens.task: Choose: Why do the passengers call him 'Mr. Know-All'?
opts: He always acts as if he knows everything.
screens.fb: The nickname makes fun of his confidence.

screens.en: Mr. Ramsay works for the American consulate in Kobe, Japan. His young wife is quiet and modest. She spent a year in New York while her husband stayed in Japan.
screens.he: מר רמזי עובד בקונסוליה האמריקאית בעיר קובה ביפן. אשתו הצעירה שקטה וצנועה. היא בילתה שנה בניו יורק, בזמן שבעלה נשאר ביפן.
screens.task: Choose: Where did Mrs. Ramsay spend the last year?
screens.fb: Remember this detail – it becomes important at the end.

screens.en: At dinner, the passengers talk about pearls. Mr. Kelada is an expert – pearls are his business. He says Mrs. Ramsay's necklace is real and very valuable. Mr. Ramsay laughs: he says it is a cheap imitation.
screens.he: בארוחת הערב הנוסעים מדברים על פנינים. מר קלדה מומחה – הוא עוסק בפנינים. הוא אומר שהשרשרת של גברת רמזי אמיתית ויקרה מאוד. מר רמזי צוחק ואומר שזו שרשרת זולה ומזויפת.
screens.task: Choose: Who thinks the pearls are real?
screens.fb: Mr. Kelada – and he is the expert.

screens.en: The two men bet a hundred dollars. Mr. Kelada takes out a magnifying glass and examines the necklace. He is about to win.
screens.he: שני הגברים מתערבים על מאה דולר. מר קלדה מוציא זכוכית מגדלת ובודק את השרשרת. הוא עומד לנצח.
screens.task: Choose: What is the bet about?
opts: who is the best card player
the price of the ship tickets
screens.fb: Whether the pearls are real or an imitation.

screens.en: Suddenly Mr. Kelada looks at Mrs. Ramsay. Her face is very pale, and her eyes beg him for help. Mr. Kelada understands.
screens.he: פתאום מר קלדה מסתכל על גברת רמזי. הפנים שלה חיוורות מאוד, והעיניים שלה מתחננות לעזרה. מר קלדה מבין.
screens.task: Choose: What clue does Mr. Kelada notice?
screens.fb: Her fear is the turning point of the story.

screens.en: Mr. Kelada says that he was wrong and that the pearls are an imitation. He pays the hundred dollars. He does this on purpose, although he knows the truth.
screens.he: מר קלדה אומר שטעה ושהפנינים מזויפות. הוא משלם מאה דולר. הוא עושה את זה בכוונה, למרות שהוא יודע את האמת.
screens.task: Why does he say he was wrong?
screens.fb: To protect Mrs. Ramsay – not because he does not know pearls.

screens.en: The story spreads around the ship. The passengers laugh at Mr. Kelada, the man who always knows everything. He loses his money and his pride.
screens.he: הסיפור מתפשט באונייה, והנוסעים צוחקים על מר קלדה – ״זה שיודע הכול״. הוא מפסיד גם כסף וגם את הכבוד שלו.
screens.task: What does Mr. Kelada lose? Name two things.
screens.fb: Money and his reputation – this makes it a real sacrifice.

screens.en: The next morning, someone pushes an envelope under the cabin door. Inside is a hundred-dollar note. Mr. Kelada hints that a young wife should not spend a year alone in New York while her husband works far away.
screens.he: למחרת בבוקר מישהו דוחף מעטפה מתחת לדלת התא, ובתוכה שטר של מאה דולר. מר קלדה רומז שאישה צעירה לא צריכה לבלות שנה לבד בניו יורק כשבעלה עובד רחוק.
screens.task: What can we infer from the envelope and the hint?
screens.fb: Mrs. Ramsay probably returned the money to thank him. The hint suggests that the pearls were a gift from another man – but this is an inference, not a fact. Do not invent who delivered the envelope.

screens.en: At the end, the narrator says that at that moment he did not entirely dislike Mr. Kelada.
screens.he: בסוף המספר אומר שבאותו רגע הוא כבר לא סלד ממר קלדה לגמרי.
screens.task: Choose: How does the narrator's opinion change?
opts: from dislike to a little respect
screens.fb: A small but important change – do not exaggerate it.

screens.en: On the outside, Mr. Kelada seems loud and arrogant. On the inside, he is kind and generous. The narrator sees the outside; the reader discovers the inside.
screens.he: מבחוץ מר קלדה נראה רעשן ויהיר. מבפנים הוא אדיב ונדיב. המספר רואה את החוץ – והקורא מגלה את הפנים.
screens.task: Complete: At first Mr. Kelada seems ____, but later we see ____.
screens.fb: Use a specific action as evidence.

screens.en: The man everyone calls 'Mr. Know-All' chooses to look as if he knows nothing. And the narrator, who thinks he knows people, is wrong about Mr. Kelada.
screens.he: אירוניה = פער בין מה שמצפים לו לבין מה שקורה באמת. האיש ש״יודע הכול״ בוחר להיראות כמי שלא יודע – והמספר, שבטוח שהוא מבין אנשים, טועה.
screens.task: Identify one irony in the story.
screens.fb: Irony is a gap between what we expect and what happens – not just a surprise.

screens.en: Fact: Mr. Kelada says the pearls are an imitation. Inference: the pearls are real, and someone else gave them to Mrs. Ramsay. The story hints, but it never says this directly.
screens.he: עובדה = כתוב בסיפור. הסקה = מבינים מהרמזים. הסיפור רק רומז מאיפה הגיעה השרשרת – הוא לא אומר את זה במפורש.
screens.task: Mark each sentence: fact or inference.
screens.fb: Separate what the story says from what we understand.

screens.en: Because the narrator tells the story, we first see Mr. Kelada as he does. The surprise at the end is our surprise too. Maugham writes in simple, clear language. The ending is short and quiet – and full of surprise.
screens.he: בגלל שהמספר מספר את הסיפור, גם אנחנו רואים קודם את מר קלדה כמו שהוא רואה אותו. ההפתעה בסוף היא גם ההפתעה שלנו. מוהם כותב בשפה פשוטה וברורה. הסוף קצר ושקט – ומלא הפתעה.
screens.task: How does the first-person narrator affect the way we see Mr. Kelada?
screens.fb: Mention both: we share his prejudice, and we share his surprise.

screens.en: Question: Why does Mr. Kelada lose the bet on purpose? Build your answer: ANSWER – PROVE – EXPLAIN.
screens.he: שאלת Why דורשת מניע – לא רק תיאור של ההתערבות.
starters: Mr. Kelada loses the bet on purpose because
screens.task: Write three sentences.
screens.fb: Model: Mr. Kelada loses the bet on purpose because he wants to protect Mrs. Ramsay. For example, he changes his answer only after he sees her pale, frightened face. This shows that her safety is more important to him than money or pride.

screens.en: A strong answer uses an event, not a general sentence like 'he is a good man'.
screens.he: ראיה טובה היא מעשה מדויק מהסיפור, לא משפט כללי כמו ״הוא אדם טוב״.
screens.task: Choose: Which event supports 'Mr. Kelada is generous'?
opts: He pays $100 and accepts the laughter.
He talks a lot at dinner.
He shares a cabin with the narrator.
screens.fb: Explain how the event proves the claim.

screens.t: From a sentence to a paragraph
screens.en: A 5-point answer is a short paragraph (about 60–100 words). Language focus: contrast words (at first, however, by the end) and character adjectives (arrogant, prejudiced, considerate, generous).
screens.he: בחמש יחידות שפה היא 50% מהציון. השתמשו במילות ניגוד ובשמות תואר לתיאור דמויות.
screens.task: Write a paragraph: How does the narrator's opinion change?
screens.fb: Feedback on content and on language (vocabulary, grammar, linking words).

screens.en: Explain how the pearl incident changes the narrator's opinion of Mr. Kelada. Write 80–100 words and use two events as evidence.
screens.he: עכשיו כותבים לבד, עם שתי ראיות. נבדוק תוכן (הבנה, ראיות, הסבר) ושפה (אוצר מילים, דקדוק, פיסוק).
screens.task: Write the paragraph; then improve it after feedback.
screens.fb: Do not state the affair as a fact. Do not say the narrator loves Mr. Kelada.

questions.q: Why does the narrator dislike Mr. Kelada at the beginning? Is his opinion fair?
questions.how: Why + Is it fair = סיבה + עמדה מנומקת.
questions.ev: The narrator's feelings before they meet; his reaction to Mr. Kelada's behavior.
questions.a: The narrator dislikes Mr. Kelada even before he meets him. He judges him by his name and his foreign origin, and later he is annoyed by his talking and his confidence. For example, he is upset that he must share a cabin with him, and almost everything Mr. Kelada does annoys him. In my opinion, this opinion is not fair, because it is based on prejudice and first impressions, not on Mr. Kelada's actions. As the story shows, the narrator does not really know him.

questions.q: What is the bet about, and why is it important?
questions.ev: The dinner conversation and the bet.
questions.a: At dinner, Mr. Kelada says that Mrs. Ramsay's pearl necklace is real and very valuable, but Mr. Ramsay says it is a cheap imitation. They bet a hundred dollars. The bet is important because it puts Mr. Kelada in a difficult situation: if he tells the truth, he wins the money but may hurt Mrs. Ramsay. As a result, the bet becomes a test of his character, not of his knowledge.

questions.q: How does Mrs. Ramsay feel when Mr. Kelada examines the pearls? How do we know?
questions.how: How does … feel = רגש + ראיה + הסקה זהירה.
questions.ev: Her pale face and pleading eyes.
questions.a: Mrs. Ramsay feels terrified. When Mr. Kelada examines the necklace, her face becomes very pale, and she looks at him as if she is begging for help. We can infer that she is afraid the truth about the pearls will come out, because her husband believes they are cheap. This moment is the turning point of the story, because Mr. Kelada sees her fear and changes his answer.

questions.q: Why does Mr. Kelada lose the bet on purpose? What does this show about him?
questions.how: Why = מניע. What does it show = תכונה.
questions.ev: He changes his answer after seeing her face; he pays and is laughed at.
questions.a: Mr. Kelada loses the bet on purpose to protect Mrs. Ramsay. He sees how frightened she is, so he says the pearls are only an imitation, even though he is an expert. He pays a hundred dollars, and the passengers laugh at him. This shows that he is kind and generous: he is ready to lose money and his reputation to save another person from trouble. In other words, he is much better than the narrator believed.

questions.q: What happens the next morning, and what can we infer from it?
questions.how: What happens + infer = עובדה + הסקה מסומנת.
questions.ev: The envelope with $100; Mr. Kelada's hint about New York.
questions.a: The next morning, someone pushes an envelope under the cabin door with a hundred-dollar note inside. We can infer that Mrs. Ramsay sent it to thank Mr. Kelada and to return his money. In addition, Mr. Kelada hints that a young wife should not spend a year alone in New York while her husband works in Japan. This suggests that someone else may have given her the pearls, but the story never says so directly.

questions.q: How does the narrator's opinion of Mr. Kelada change?
questions.ev: His first feelings; his last sentence.
questions.a: At the beginning, the narrator dislikes Mr. Kelada and finds him annoying and arrogant. At the end, after he sees Mr. Kelada's sacrifice, he admits that at that moment he did not entirely dislike him. This change is small but important. It shows that Mr. Kelada's actions made the narrator question his first impression. However, the narrator does not say that he likes him, so we should not exaggerate the change.

questions.q: The story is told by a first-person narrator. How does this affect the way we see Mr. Kelada?
questions.how: Form/style = איך הסיפור מסופר ומה זה עושה לקורא.
questions.ev: The narrator's early descriptions; the surprise at the end.
questions.a: Because the story is told by the narrator, we see Mr. Kelada through his prejudiced eyes. At first, we also find Mr. Kelada annoying, because the narrator describes mainly his loud talking and his confidence. Later, we discover, together with the narrator, that Mr. Kelada is generous. I appreciated this technique, because it makes the reader feel the same surprise, and it shows how easily we judge people. It also makes us ask whether we can trust the narrator.

questions.q: Explain the irony of the title "Mr. Know-All."
questions.ev: The nickname; the false admission at the bet.
questions.a: The title is ironic. The passengers call Mr. Kelada "Mr. Know-All" to make fun of him, because he always has an answer. However, in the most important moment, he chooses to look as if he knows nothing about pearls. He knows the truth, but he hides it to protect Mrs. Ramsay. In addition, it is the narrator, not Mr. Kelada, who thinks he knows everything about people – and he is wrong. That is why the title gets a new meaning at the end.

mistakes: Mr. Kelada lost because he did not know pearls.
He gives the wrong answer on purpose after he sees Mrs. Ramsay's fear.
The story proves that Mrs. Ramsay had an affair.
This is an inference from a hint, not a fact.
The narrator loves Mr. Kelada at the end.
He only says that at that moment he did not entirely dislike him.
He also lost his pride: the passengers laugh at him.
stories.bridging: Bridging text and context: after World War I, many people judged others by their nationality and origin. Write 80–100 words: How does the narrator's prejudice reflect the attitudes of his time, and is it still relevant today? (CD4, CD7)

compare.q: Compare Mr. Cattanzara and Mr. Kelada. How are they similar, and how are they different?
compare.a: Both men protect someone's dignity by hiding the truth. Mr. Cattanzara knows that George has not read the books, but it seems that he tells the neighbors George finished them. Similarly, Mr. Kelada knows the pearls are real, but he says they are fake to protect Mrs. Ramsay. However, their goals are different: Mr. Cattanzara wants to push George to change, while Mr. Kelada wants to save Mrs. Ramsay from trouble. In both stories, a kind lie shows the goodness of a character.

compare.q: Compare how respect works in the two stories.
compare.a: In both stories, respect is connected to how other people see us. George enjoys respect that he has not earned, because people believe a lie about him. In contrast, Mr. Kelada does not get respect at first, although he deserves it, because the narrator judges him by his origin. In the end, both stories suggest that real respect comes from actions: George starts to earn it at the library, and Mr. Kelada earns the narrator's respect through his sacrifice.
